question: The mean of a data is 43 and its median is 78. The mode (using empirical relation) of the data is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Apply the **Empirical Formula**: **Mode** = 3 × **Median** − 2 × **Mean**.

Substitute the given values: **Mode** = 3(78) − 2(43).

**Mode** = 234 − 86 = 148.

**∴ The correct answer is 148.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Mean** = 43

**Median** = 78

**Formula Used:**

The **empirical relationship** between the three measures of central tendency is:

**Mode** = 3 × **Median** − 2 × **Mean**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/838d338c78506e4f480b75a66166fe99987934973f431d6000f27157b3a46003.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Mode** = 3 × 78 − 2 × 43

⇒ **Mode** = 234 − 86

⇒ **Mode** = 148

**∴ The correct answer is 148.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Empirical Relationship

This formula is an approximation used for **moderately skewed** distributions. It is also known as **Karl Pearson's formula**.

Symmetrical Distribution

In a perfectly **symmetrical distribution** (like a Normal Distribution), the Mean, Median, and Mode are all equal (**Mean = Median = Mode**).

Skewness and Central Tendency

For a **positively skewed** distribution, Mean > Median > Mode. For a **negatively skewed** distribution, Mean < Median < Mode.</p
